messages:
acme_devops: Hey team — we started a large data migration at 09:12 UTC and clients are seeing intermittent 429s + a few 401s. It started right after we rotated our API keys. We hit ~25k requests in 10 minutes. Can you help?

sam_support: Sorry about that — can you share the project/org id and the exact error payload if possible? 429 or 401? Any retry spikes?

acme_devops: Mostly 429, about 5% 401 during a ~2 minute window. Example error: `{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":30}`. We do tens of parallel workers that retried aggressively. Org: acme-123, plan: free.

lee_oncall: Thanks — this looks like a classic key-rotation -> retry stampede. When keys rotated, some clients got 401, retried, hit backoff code that retried immediately, causing burst above per-minute cap. Free tier has per-minute and per-day soft caps.

sam_support: Quick mitigation: 1) Pause the import clients (if possible) 2) Reduce parallelism to <= 8 workers and add randomized backoff (jitter) 3) Confirm new key is propagated and stop retry loops.

acme_devops: We're pausing for now. Can Redwood temporarily raise the per-minute cap while we finish the import? This is a scheduled one-off migration.

maya_sales: Happy to help with a temporary bridge. For free-tier customers we can offer a 24–72h paid trial uplift (sales-assisted). I can start a short-term paid upgrade if legal/billing ok. What's the required RPS?

acme_devops: Need roughly 45 requests/sec sustained for 3 hours. Total tokens modest — mostly metadata calls.

lee_oncall: ECN: 45 RPS aggregated will exceed free tier burst rules. Technically we can route you to a temporary uplift, but we need billing signoff because it's a usage bump. In the meantime, if you can't upgrade right now, implement batching to reduce call rate (we have embed endpoints that accept multiple items per request).

sam_support: Also confirming auth problem: when rotating keys ensure the old key is accepted with a short overlap window and clients use exponential backoff: e.g., 1s, 2s, 4s + random_jitter. Avoid tight loops `while(401) retry immediately` patterns.

acme_devops: Understood. Can you repro the 401 -> 429 pattern on your side? We have logs and will paste a short trace.

sam_support: Yes, we can simulate. Please paste one of the error traces and the curl you used. Example repro curl we use: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/text/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"hi"}'``` Replace with your project headers.

acme_devops: Pasted: `service-worker` showed `401` at 09:13:01, then retry fired 6x within 18s, then service-level backpressure triggered and returned 429s 09:13:22->09:15:30.

lee_oncall: That's consistent. Two action paths: A) Sales uplift now so we can raise limits for a short window (maya to action), B) engineering mitigation + best-practice code changes (sam guidance). For fast lift, Maya — can you start an invoice/charge for 48h uplift and set limits to 60 RPS?

maya_sales: I can. I'll create a short-term uplift order for 48h at equivalent of paid starter tier and route to billing for approval. @billing_bot please provision temporary 60 RPS for org acme-123 once payment is live.

billing_bot: Received uplift request: org=acme-123, uplift=60RPS, duration=48h. Awaiting billing confirmation.

acme_devops: Thank you. We'll also roll a short client patch this morning to add exponential backoff and reduce threads. Any recommended SDK timeout/backoff params?

sam_support: Recommended: base=500ms, multiplier=2, max=8s, jitter=50%. Increase client-side circuit-breaker to stop after 5 failures for 30s. Also enable bulk endpoints if you can to cut request count by ~4x.

acme_devops: Great — implementing now. Will confirm once uplift is live and we finish import.

lee_oncall: Follow-ups: - Eng to simulate token-rotation + retry stampede to create a short KB note. - Support to confirm uplift once billing_bot signals done. - Customer to report any lingering 429s after patch.

sam_support: I'll file a short KB with repro steps and code snippets under support playbooks. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
